## Y8960 Sequencer BIOS

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../sequencer-bios.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

The firmware for the Y8960 cartridge has four independent sequencers for automatic playback. To make this function available to application software other than the BASIC extension (DOS, ROM cartridges, etc.) as well, it publishes BIOS entries.
The Y8960 BASIC Extension always treats each sequencer and its sequence data as 1:1, but the Y8960 Sequencer BIOS assumes that the user application manages the sequence data, and any sequence data can be allocated to a sequencer.

The Y8960 BASIC Extension also uses these BIOS entries internally. (Its internal routines are published as the Sequencer BIOS.)

### How to reach it

The Sequencer BIOS is in the resident part (ROM #4) of the Y8960 BASIC Extension, and cannot be called unless the resident part is switched into BANK0. At power-on a different ROM is switched in, so the application first switches the resident part in with the MSX Sound Suite attach entry.
For the procedure, see "Use from applications" in [`msse-abi.md`](msse-abi.md).

1. Select page 1 of every slot in turn, and find the slot where `4000h` holds `'AB'` and `4010h` holds `'MSSE8960'`
2. `CALLSLT` that slot's `4060h` with `A` = 2 (Y8960 BASIC Extension)
3. If CY is not set, the resident part is switched into BANK0. From then on, the entries below can be called with `CALLSLT` to the same slot

Once the attach has succeeded, it is certain that this is the resident part, so the Sequencer BIOS has no signature of its own.

### Memory map

In the first half of the resident part (the BANK0 window, `4000h`-`5FFFh`), the fixed addresses are as follows.

| Address | Contents |
|---|---|
| `4000h`-`400Fh` | MSX cartridge header. `400Ah` is the `XBTAB` pointer |
| `4010h`-`401Fh` | MSX Sound Suite signature `'MSSE8960'`. From `4018h` on, spare for MSX Sound Suite |
| `4020h`-`403Fh` | Resident part signature |
| `4040h`-`404Fh` | Version string |
| `4050h`-`405Fh` | Sequencer BIOS information block |
| `4060h`-`406Fh` | Reserved for MSX Sound Suite. `4060h` is the attach entry |
| `4070h`-`40FFh` | Sequencer BIOS jump table |
| `4100h`- | Code |

The jump table reserves room for 48 entries. Entries may only be added by appending at the end. Inserting one in the middle would make existing applications call a different entry.

**All 48 entries are filled.** Implemented entries jump to their implementation; the others jump to a stub that just returns with CY set. Wherever in the reserved area you call, nothing else is ever executed. Which entries are implemented can be found out by calling them and looking at CY.

#### Information block

Publishes values that an application cannot hard-code.

| Offset | Length | Contents |
|--:|--:|---|
| +0 | 1 | Sequencer BIOS ABI version |
| +1 | 1 | Spare |
| +2 | 2 | Number of bytes of work area that `SQINIT` requires |
| +4 | 12 | Reserved |

The size of the work area grows as implementation progresses. Read it from here so that the application never embeds the value.

The current ABI version is 8.

### BIOS entry list

| Address | Entry | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `4070h` | SQINIT | Prepares the hook and work area and makes the sequencer ready for use |
| `4073h` | SQEXIT | Releases the hook and work area and returns to the state before `SQINIT` |
| `4076h` | SQALLC | Allocates sequence data to a sequencer |
| `4079h` | SQFREE | Releases a sequencer |
| `407Ch` | SQSTRT | Starts sequencer playback |
| `407Fh` | SQPAUS | Pauses sequencer playback |
| `4082h` | SQSTOP | Stops sequencer playback |
| `4085h` | SQMUTE | Mutes sequencer playback |
| `4088h` | SQSTAT | Gets the playback state of a sequencer |
| `408Bh` | SQSCCW | Writes an SCC register |
| `408Eh` | SQSCCR | Reads an SCC register |
| `4091h` | SQMIX | Sets the hardware mixer |
| `4094h` | SQVOL | Sets the playback volume per sequence |
| `4097h` | SQPTBR | Reads the ADPCM voice file settings into main RAM |
| `409Ah` | SQPTBW | Replaces the ADPCM voice file settings with settings in main RAM |
| `409Dh` | SQPCMR | Reads the contents of ADPCM memory into main RAM |
| `40A0h` | SQPCMW | Writes the contents of main RAM into ADPCM memory |

`SQFREE` is the counterpart of `SQALLC` and removes the allocation of one sequencer. Returning the hook and work area and finishing the use of the BIOS itself is done by `SQEXIT`.

`SQMIX` and `SQVOL` set different things. `SQMIX` is the Digital Mixer in the FPGA itself and decides the output level of each block. `SQVOL` is the playback volume of one sequence and lowers the volume of all the channels that sequence uses together. The `SQSTOP` fade-out lowers the latter and does not affect the mixer settings.

### BIOS entry details

#### Common conventions

- Calls are made with `CALLSLT` (`RST 30h`). `CALLSLT` itself destroys `IY`
- Unless stated otherwise, all registers are destroyed
- Success or failure is returned in CY. CY clear is success. **No reason code is returned**
- The resident part must be switched into BANK0. If it is not, call the MSX Sound Suite attach entry first
- Entries that take a sequence receive it in `A`. A one-byte argument that goes with it is in `B`
- **The `A` of `SQSTRT` `SQPAUS` `SQSTOP` `SQMUTE` is a bitmap**: bit n is sequence n (`01h` is sequence 0, `05h` is sequences 0 and 2). 0, and values with any of bits 4-7 set, give CY. The specified sequences are all acted on without playback advancing even once in between. **If even one of them meets a condition for refusal, CY is returned and none of the sequences change.** For the other entries, `A` is a sequence number (0-3)
- **Call with interrupts enabled. They are enabled on return as well.** Entries that touch a playing sequence use the same work area as the interrupt handler, so they disable interrupts only while they are touching it

#### SQINIT — enable the sequencer

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4070h` |
| Input | `HL` = start of the work area<br>`B` = tick resolution (0 / 1 / 2 = 60 / 100 / 200Hz, see below)<br>`D` `E` = not used (panning is set per channel by the sequence's `87` (`i`*n* in MML), and rhythm mode is decided by `SQSTRT`) |
| Output | CY set = `SQINIT` has already been done, the work area is below `C000h`, **the stack at the time of the call is below `C000h`**, or `B` is greater than 2. In every case nothing has been changed |

Records the work area, enables the regular I/O ports, initializes the control blocks, resets all devices and **takes over an interrupt hook** (`B` decides which one; see below).

##### Tick resolution

The sequencer keeps time with a periodic interrupt. `B` selects that period. **The period translates directly into the load the application sees** — the cost of the music itself is the same at every setting, but the fixed cost per interrupt is paid once for every interrupt.

| `B` | Period | Interrupt source | Hook taken over |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 60Hz (50Hz on PAL machines) | Rides on the VDP interrupt | `H.TIMI` |
| 1 | About 100Hz | MSX-TIMER | `H.KEYI` |
| 2 | About 200Hz | MSX-TIMER | `H.KEYI` |

**`B`=0 causes no additional interrupts.** It only rides on the VDP interrupt that happens anyway, so the application pays only for the sequencer's processing itself. **In exchange, the time granularity is 1/60 second**, and short notes at fast tempos fall onto that grid.

**`B`=2 is the finest and the heaviest.** It adds 200 interrupts per second.

**With `B`=0 the MSX-TIMER is not used.** This avoids running two interrupt sources with similar periods in parallel.

**The application provides the work area.** The required number of bytes is given at +2 of the information block. This value grows as implementation progresses, so read it instead of embedding it.

**The work area must be placed in `C000h`-`FFFFh`.** Page 1 is switched to the cartridge during BIOS calls and interrupts, page 0 is MAIN-ROM during interrupt handling, and page 2 is the cartridge during interrupt handling. Wherever in those pages it is placed, it is not visible at the moment the sequencer reads the work area.

**Put the stack in `C000h`-`FFFFh` as well.** The reason is the same: page 2 is switched during interrupts. A program that takes its work area below `HIMEM` gets this naturally.

**Until you call `SQEXIT`, do not give up or overwrite this area.** The sequencer reads it on every interrupt.

#### SQEXIT — finish using the sequencer

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4073h` |
| Input | None |
| Output | CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed, or the hook it took over ("Tick resolution") now belongs to someone else. In either case nothing has been changed |

Stops all sequencers, restores the hook it took over, silences the sound chips and disables the regular I/O ports. The work area belongs to the application again.

The I/O ports are not disabled just for tidiness. The ports handed out here are the same ones the MSX computer uses for its own hardware — `A0h`/`A1h` for the PSG, `7Ch`/`7Dh` for MSX-MUSIC — so if they stayed enabled, the cartridge's sound chips would also respond to writes to them.

**Only the OPL2EX ports (`C0h`/`C1h`) are touched by neither `SQINIT` nor `SQEXIT`.** At cartridge startup they are enabled if there is no MSX-AUDIO at `C0h`, and they stay enabled ("OPL2EX stays enabled from startup" in [`msse-abi.md`](msse-abi.md)). When an MSX-AUDIO is present they are not enabled, so the OPL2EX does not sound, and writes to `C0h` reach that MSX-AUDIO.

#### SQSTRT — play sequences

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `407Ch` |
| Input | `A` = sequence bitmap<br>`B` = repeat count (0 is infinite; the value equivalent to omitting it is 1) |
| Output | CY set = the bitmap is out of range, `SQINIT` has not been executed, or one of the specified sequences has no playback data |

A paused sequence resumes from the point where it was paused, and in that case the repeat count is not taken again. Otherwise the sequence starts from the beginning and its sequence volume is reset to the `SQVOL` value (so that a sequence that went down to 0 in a fade-out does not start silent the next time).

When starting from the beginning, **the first tick is processed inside this entry**. The first note is already sounding before `SQSTRT` returns. On resume, no tick is processed here.

**When starting from the beginning, it also decides the rhythm mode of each OPLLEX and OPL2EX block.**
A block that has a track on channel 10 enters rhythm mode, and a block that has a track on channels 6-8 leaves rhythm mode. A block that has neither is left as it is. When entering rhythm mode, the F-Numbers of channels 6-8 and the volumes of the rhythm sounds are set to their defaults, and on the OPL2EX the rhythm voices are loaded into channels 6-8. On resume and
when going back to the beginning on a repeat, these are not set again, so values rewritten with `Y` during playback remain. Right after `SQINIT`, no block is in rhythm mode.

The repeat count goes down by one when all tracks have reached their end. When it reaches 0, the sequence stops (0 in `SQSTAT`).

#### SQPAUS — pause sequences

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `407Fh` |
| Input | `A` = sequence bitmap |
| Output | CY set = the bitmap is out of range, `SQINIT` has not been executed, or one of the specified sequences is not playing |

Keys off the channels the sequence is using and leaves the read position where it is. `SQSTRT` continues from the same place.

#### SQSTOP — stop sequences

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4082h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence bitmap<br>`B` = fade-out time in seconds (0-127, 0 is immediate) |
| Output | CY set = the bitmap is out of range, or `SQINIT` has not been executed |

If the number of seconds is 0, the channels are keyed off on the spot and the sequence stops (0 in `SQSTAT`). Otherwise it moves to fading out (3 in `SQSTAT`), lowers the sequence volume to 0 over that many seconds, and stops when it reaches 0. **What goes down is the sequence volume; the `SQMIX` settings are not affected.**

The seconds are counted in interrupts, not ticks, so **changing the tempo does not change the length**.

#### SQMUTE — mute sequences

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4085h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence bitmap<br>`B` = 0 to unmute, anything else to mute |
| Output | CY set = the bitmap is out of range, `SQINIT` has not been executed, or one of the specified sequences is not playing |

A muted sequence keeps advancing. Only the sound is suppressed: no key-on happens, and volume writes are replaced with the value that means silence. When unmuted, sound comes out from the playback position at that moment.

#### SQSTAT — get the state of a sequence

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4088h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence number (0-3) |
| Output | `A` = state<br>CY set = the sequence number is out of range, or `SQINIT` has not been executed |

| Value | State |
|--:|---|
| 0 | Stopped |
| 1 | Playing |
| 2 | Paused (`SQPAUS`) |
| 3 | Fading out (seconds given to `SQSTOP`) |

`CALL MSTAT` only answers "1 if playing", so **only this entry can tell stopped from paused**. To check only whether a sequence is playing, compare with 1.

#### SQVOL — set a sequence's playback volume

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4094h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence number (0-3)<br>`B` = volume (0-127) |
| Output | CY set = the sequence number is out of range |

Sets how much the volume of all the channels the sequence uses is lowered together. Each channel sounds at the MML volume (0-127) minus (127 − `B`), and at 0 if that goes below 0. The volume rules are the same as `VOLUME` in `basic-reference.md`. The hardware mixer settings do not change.

It can also be set for a sequence that is not playing, and becomes the volume the next time `SQSTRT` is called. If it is set during a `SQSTOP` fade-out, the fade starts again from the set value toward 0.

#### SQMIX — set the hardware mixer

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4091h` |
| Input | `HL` = 6 bytes in total: 1 master byte + 5 block bytes (each 0-128) |
| Output | CY set = the 6 bytes do not fit within `8000h`-`FFFFh`, or a value exceeds 128. In every case nothing has been changed |

The blocks are in the order SSGS, OPLLEX, OPL2EX, SCC, OPM. All six are set together, so to change just one, the application rewrites its own 6 bytes and calls again.

The six values are written as they are to the Digital Mixer's overall volume register and per-block volume registers. 0 is silent, 128 is maximum.

**It can be called even if `SQINIT` has not been executed.** This is because the mixer is not state of this BIOS but the cartridge's registers themselves. For the same reason, `SQINIT` and `SQEXIT` do not touch the mixer.

**All six go back to 128 when a ROM is switched in with the MSX Sound Suite attach entry.** They go back both when this ROM is attached and when the MSX-MUSIC, MSX-AUDIO or OPM BASIC extension is attached, so make the settings after attaching this ROM. Attaching the MIDI Play BASIC Extension does not reset them.

#### SQSCCW — write an SCC register

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `408Bh` |
| Input | `A` = register offset (`00h`-`FFh`)<br>`B` = value to write |
| Output | CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed |

#### SQSCCR — read an SCC register

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `408Eh` |
| Input | `A` = register offset (`00h`-`FFh`) |
| Output | `B` = value<br>CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed |

The offset is **the raw value from the start of the SCC register block**; the BIOS does not translate it.

| Offset | Contents |
|---|---|
| `00h`-`7Fh` | Waveform memory. 32 bytes × 4 blocks. CH3 and CH4 share the last block |
| `80h`-`89h` | Frequency. 2 bytes per channel × 5 channels |
| `8Ah`-`8Eh` | Volume. 5 channels, 0-15 |
| `8Fh` | Channel ON/OFF. bit0-4 |
| `E0h`-`FFh` | deformation register |

**SCC panning is not in this range and cannot be written with `SQSCCW`.** Panning is set with the sequence's panpot (`87`). `SQINIT` sets all 5 channels to center.

For what reading and writing mean, see "Memory constraints" below.

#### SQALLC — allocate sequence data

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4076h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence number (0-3)<br>`HL` = start of the sequence data<br>`B` = 0 take ownership / 1 play in place |
| Output | CY set = the sequence number or `B` is out of range, `SQINIT` has not been executed, the data is not in this format, the length given by the header exceeds `FFFFh`, the sequence already has tracks, another sequence holds a requested channel, or channel 10 and channels 6-8 of the same OPLLEX or OPL2EX block come together (whether between this and another sequence or within the data alone) |

The data format is "Block" in [`bytecode.md`](bytecode.md). **The length is not passed**
— the header carries it.

**`B`=0 is the straightforward way to use it.** The data is copied to cartridge RAM, so the buffer you passed belongs to the application again as soon as the call returns.

**`B`=1 does not copy.** The tracks read the memory passed in directly, so the data must be placed in `C000h`-`FFFFh`, and must not be moved or overwritten until `SQFREE`.

**On failure, nothing has changed.** Channel conflicts are resolved by inspecting the data once before allocating, so it never ends up partly allocated.

#### SQFREE — release sequence data

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4079h` |
| Input | `A` = sequence number (0-3) |
| Output | CY set = the sequence number is out of range, or `SQINIT` has not been executed |

Stops the sequence and gives back the channels of all its tracks. Data that `SQALLC` took ownership of is discarded here, and data that was being played in place belongs to the application again. Specifying a sequence that has no tracks is not an error.

#### SQPTBR — read the ADPCM voice file settings

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `4097h` |
| Input | `HL` = where to write the settings (448 bytes) |
| Output | `A` = number of entries, `DE` = number of ADPCM memory pages in use<br>CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed, or the 448 bytes from `HL` do not fit within `8000h`-`FFFFh` |

Writes the settings of the voice files placed in ADPCM memory, 7 bytes per entry. An entry is the voice file number (1 byte), the start page (2 bytes), the number of pages (2 bytes) and the sampling frequency in Hz (2 bytes) (low byte first). **This is the same layout as the contents of chunk `03` in sequence data**, and a page is 256 bytes. Only `A` entries are written, but there can be up to 64, so 448 bytes of space are needed.

The number of pages in use is the page after the last page that any voice file reaches. Reading ADPCM memory from the start up to there with `SQPCMR` captures every voice file placed there.

#### SQPTBW — write the ADPCM voice file settings

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `409Ah` |
| Input | `HL` = settings (same layout as `SQPTBR`), `A` = number of entries (0-64) |
| Output | CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed, the number of entries is out of range, the settings do not fit within `8000h`-`FFFFh`, a value is invalid (a number of 64 or more, a page count of 0, extending outside ADPCM memory, a frequency outside 1800-16000Hz), or a sequence or `MPLAY` is playing. In every case nothing has been changed |

**Replaces all the voice file settings.** Numbers that are not in the settings end up with no settings. All values are checked before anything is written, so if even one entry is invalid, nothing changes. If the same number appears twice, the later one remains. The contents of ADPCM memory are not touched.

While playing (except while paused), CY is returned. This is so as not to change settings that a playing ADPCM track is reading.

#### SQPCMR — read ADPCM memory

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `409Dh` |
| Input | `HL` = destination, `DE` = start page, `BC` = number of pages (0-128) |
| Output | CY set = `SQINIT` has not been executed, the number of pages exceeds 128, the range extends outside ADPCM memory (start page + number of pages exceeds 1024), or the destination does not fit within `8000h`-`FFFFh` |

Writes `BC` pages starting at ADPCM memory page `DE` to memory starting at `HL`. One page is 256 bytes. It can be called while playing, but ADPCM channel sounds may drop out meanwhile.

#### SQPCMW — write ADPCM memory

| | |
|---|---|
| Address | `40A0h` |
| Input | `HL` = data to write, `DE` = start page, `BC` = number of pages (0-128) |
| Output | CY set = the same conditions as `SQPCMR`, or a sequence or `MPLAY` is playing. In every case nothing has been changed |

Writes `BC` pages from `HL` into ADPCM memory starting at page `DE`.

**For all four entries, the main RAM is `8000h`-`FFFFh`.** During the call, page 0 is MAIN-ROM and page 1 is this cartridge, so those cannot be read or written. Page 2 is used as whatever the application has switched in.

The file that BASIC's `CALL EXPORT PCM` writes consists of a header followed by these settings and the contents of ADPCM memory; its layout is in [`basic-reference.md`](basic-reference.md). An application can read and write the same file by combining the four entries.

### Where sequence data lives

Sequence data **can be placed either in cartridge RAM banks or in main RAM**. When the bank number in the track control block is 0, it refers to main RAM; otherwise it refers to a cartridge RAM bank. Bank #0 is ROM, so it can never be a track buffer, and that value is free.

| | Cartridge RAM bank | Main RAM |
|---|---|---|
| Where it can go | 120KB in #17-#31 | `C000h`-`FFFFh` |
| Who prepares it | `SQALLC` takes ownership | The application |
| After passing it | The buffer may be released | Cannot be given up until `SQFREE` |

**Passing it to `SQALLC` is the straightforward way.** It reads the application's buffer and copies it to cartridge RAM banks, so **the buffer can be anywhere the application can read**, and it can be released right after passing it. What was read from disk can be passed as it is.

**When placed in main RAM, it must be in `C000h`-`FFFFh`.** The reason is the same as for the `SQINIT` work area: pages 0, 1 and 2 hold something else at the moment the sequencer reads. **This is a route for small songs you want to play without copying**; there is not much free space in page 3 once the stack and work area are excluded.

A track's data is placed entirely in one place. The player only decides, at the entry of track processing, whether to switch in a bank, and after that reads uniformly.

### Sequence data format

The format that `SQALLC` receives is identical to what the Y8960 BASIC Extension's `MSAVE` writes and `MLOAD` reads. **There is only one format for serialized sequence data**, and data saved with `MSAVE` can be passed to `SQALLC` as it is.

This format includes the device and channel assignment of each track. This is because what `SQALLC` needs in order to bind data to a sequencer is the same as what `MLOAD` needs in order to detect overlap with existing assignments.

**The FM voice data and SCC waveform data that a sequence uses are included in the block.** Everything needed for playback is present in the sequence data alone, so the application does not need to manage voices or waveforms separately and register them in advance. The same goes for tracks that use ROM presets: their records are included in the block. **The same also goes for tracks that select no voice**: the record of the default voice 0, which the first note plays, is included in the block.

**Things for which a number is enough are not included.** OPLLEX built-in voices and SSGS settings have no records, because the chip itself resolves them by number.

The byte-level definition is "Block" in [`bytecode.md`](bytecode.md).

**A block that has voices uses one of the sequencer's internal buffers.** Even when the data is passed so that `SQALLC` plays it in place, the voice records alone are copied inside. The buffer is given back by `SQFREE`. **The same goes for software envelope records**: a block with no voices still uses one internal buffer if it has envelopes.

**ADPCM samples are not included in the block.** They live in the 256KB sample memory, so putting them in the block would cause a transfer every time it is passed. An application that plays a sequence using ADPCM must **prepare voice files with the same numbers itself** (from the BIOS with `SQPTBW` and `SQPCMW`; from BASIC with `CALL IMPORT PCM`, or with `CALL SET PCM` and `CALL COPY PCM`). For the voice files used by the sequence that were in sample memory, the block contains a record of their location, length and sampling frequency. `SQALLC` does not use it, so keeping the contents of the sample memory consistent with this record is the application's responsibility.

**The OPL2EX rhythm voices are also included in the block**, but `SQALLC` does not use them. When entering rhythm mode (`SQSTRT`), the voices in ROM are loaded.

### Memory constraints

While the sequencer is running, the user application **must not switch any of BANK0, BANK1, BANK2 or BANK3**. **It must not change the slot of page 2 either** — during interrupts the sequencer switches it to the cartridge, uses it, and switches it back. For the reason and the general form, see "Restrictions while a ROM that hooks interrupts is in use" in [`msse-abi.md`](msse-abi.md).

This constraint directly affects the SCC. **The SCC alone has no regular I/O ports, and its registers cannot be touched unless they are switched into the BANK1 window**. Therefore, while the sequencer is running, the user application cannot control the SCC directly. Always control the SCC through `SQSCCW` / `SQSCCR`.

**What `SQSCCR` returns is not the chip's value but the shadow held by the driver.** The SCC's frequency, volume and channel ON/OFF registers are write-only and cannot be read. `SQSCCW` updates the shadow at the same time as it writes, and the sequencer itself also goes through the same shadow when it writes to the SCC. Therefore the shadow matches the value last written to the chip, regardless of who wrote it.

The initial value of the shadow is the state after `SQINIT` has reset the SCC, that is, **frequency, volume and channel ON/OFF all 0, with waveform 0 in all four waveform blocks**. It is not the chip's value right after power-on.

Read and write sequence data while the sequencer is stopped.

### Chaining interrupt hooks

The sequencer takes over the hook chosen by the resolution (`H.KEYI` or `H.TIMI`; "Tick resolution") with an inter-slot call in `RST 30h` form. This is why it reaches the resident part no matter what is in page 1 at the moment of the interrupt.

**If the application has its own interrupt handling, install and remove hooks in LIFO order.**

- Call `SQINIT`, then install your own hook
- Remove your own hook, then call `SQEXIT`

In this order, the application may put its hook body in its own slot's ROM in page 1 and jump there directly with `JP`. This is because the interrupt enters the application's hook first, and at that time page 1 is still the application's slot.

`SQEXIT` fails if the hook it took over is not its own. If it erased a hook installed later by writing the old one back, there would be no way to restore the hook that dropped out of the chain.

#### Hooking in reverse order

A hook installed before `SQINIT` is called from inside the sequencer's interrupt handling. At that time page 1 has been switched to the Y8960's slot, so **where the hook body is placed matters**.

| Where the hook body is placed | Does the chain reach it |
|---|---|
| Page 3 (main RAM) | Reaches it |
| Page 2 (`8000h`-`BFFFh`) | Reaches it. `RST 30h` switches only page 1 |
| Page 1, with a direct `JP` | **Does not reach it**. It jumps to the same address in the Y8960 |
| Page 1, in `RST 30h` form | Reaches it |
| Page 0 | Does not reach it. It is MAIN-ROM during interrupt handling |

If you really must install your hook before `SQINIT`, put the hook body in page 2 or main RAM, or install your hook in `RST 30h` form as well.

### Accessing the sound devices while the sequencer runs

The sequencer accesses the sound devices only from inside the chain of the hook it took over. If the user application operates the sound devices directly, it must access them from inside the same chain, or with interrupts disabled. Behavior is not guaranteed if the application directly operates the sound devices and channels that the sequencer uses. (Mutual exclusion of devices and channels is the application's responsibility.)
